about.title: Technology with a human face
paragraphs: DeepKind Foundation started from a simple belief: in a world of constant change, we need new ways of thinking, rooted in empathy, care and the responsible use of technology. We work across education, the humanities and innovation, building spaces where thinking and doing meet.

Care for people is at the heart of everything we do: their wellbeing, their relationships, their sense of agency. We believe technology should strengthen people, not override them. We connect different perspectives and partners to create lasting change that means something.
DeepKind is a space where kindness becomes practice, and responsibility becomes the foundation of the future.
about.quote: We build initiatives that connect people, technology and care, creating a movement that inspires living with energy, empathy and mindfulness.

items.question: What is DeepKind Foundation?
items.answer: DeepKind Foundation is an initiative bridging technology, the humanities and education. We build spaces where technological development goes hand in hand with care for people, their wellbeing and their relationships.

items.question: Why does technology need more mindfulness today?
items.answer: Because its impact goes far beyond what it does on screen. It shapes how we think, work and relate to each other. Being mindful means designing things that support people rather than wear them out.

items.question: What does "technology that serves" mean to you?
items.answer: Technology built with the human in mind: their wellbeing, their abilities and their limits. Not just clever, but responsible.

items.question: Who do you work with?
items.answer: People in tech and business, women finding their footing, young adults, children and families. We also partner with organisations and companies.

items.question: How can I get involved?
items.answer: You can volunteer, support us financially, or partner with us. Every bit helps and makes a real difference to what we can do.

items.question: Are participation fees required?
items.answer: Many of our programmes are free, especially those for children, young adults and communities. Some initiatives have a cost; we always say so upfront for each project.

items.question: Why do you combine technology with the humanities?
items.answer: Because technical skills alone aren't enough to deal with the complex problems of today. You also need ethics, reflection and a genuine understanding of people: their feelings, their motivations, their context.

items.question: What makes your approach to leadership different?
items.answer: We care about balance rather than constant speed. We think good leadership starts with knowing yourself, and that's what shapes your decisions, your team and your organisation.

items.question: Is this only for people in tech?
items.answer: No. Technology is part of the context, but our work is for anyone who wants to act with more intention, whatever field they're in.

items.question: Do you work with companies and organisations?
items.answer: Yes. We partner with organisations that want to act responsibly and create something with real social and environmental value.

items.question: Where are you based?
items.answer: We're based in Poland, but some of our work and collaborations cross borders.

items.question: What kind of change are you after?
items.answer: The kind that lasts and actually means something, not just fast and surface-level. Change that gives people more room, builds real connections and makes work and life a bit healthier.
